Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 3 days of frequent watery diarrhea and intermittent left lower abdominal cramps after recent takeaway; initial vomiting and subjective fever; suspected acute gastroenteritis. Conservative management advised with hydration, ORS, analgesia, rest, and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of watery, loose stools, ~6–7 times/day; intermittent cramp-like left lower abdominal pain.
- Associated symptoms: Initial vomiting (now resolved); felt hot/subjective fever at onset (no measured temperature); weakness/shakiness; reduced appetite; able to keep fluids down. No blood in stool or vomit.
- Pertinent negatives: No ongoing vomiting; no blood in stools; pain does not radiate to back.
- Triggers/exposures: Ate at a Chinese restaurant 4 days ago; one child vomited but no diarrhea; no similar illness in others at home.
- Past medical history: Asthma, well-controlled.
- Medications: Asthma inhaler (name/dose/route/frequency not documented). No other medications.
- Social history: Lives with wife and two children; accountant; continued working despite symptoms; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:

Impression:
- Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral; bacterial etiology possible). No red flags reported; dehydration risk considered.

Plan:
- Hydration: Encourage liberal oral fluids.
- Oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) recommended, especially over the first couple of days (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Analgesia/antipyretic: Paracetamol “two tablets up to four times daily” for a few days if feverish/weak; specific tablet strength and route not documented.
- Rest: Advise 2–3 days off work to recover.
- Antibiotics: Not indicated at this stage.
- Follow-up: If symptoms do not improve in 3–4 days, return for reevaluation; stool testing may be arranged if ongoing.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies; detailed medication reconciliation (including inhaler name/strength/route/frequency); vitals; physical exam; assessment of hydration status; travel history/recent antibiotic use; infection control advice not discussed.
- Internal conflicts: Patient initially denied vomiting, later reported vomiting at symptom onset but now resolved (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor repetitions and interruptions.
